| o33_wrapper_classification_residuals | AMENDED, narrowed to what is left after the third repair. Three of the four items are closed in codes/loop/loop.sbatch and one is documented as intended. CLOSED (a): a SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight now stops the wrapper before the loop is launched -- SCHED_TERM is tested immediately above the launch, the wrapper says so, exits 143 and finalize books a scheduler termination with the count untouched and the successor kept (probe (i)-b: BEFORE the stand-in printed 'LOOP RAN AFTER THE SIGNAL' and the link exited 0; AFTER 'SIGTERM already received during the pre-flight -- not starting the loop', wrapper exit 143). CLOSED (b, the after-the-fact half): the loop's own status is recorded into LOOP_RC the instant it is known, on_term records whether that recording had already happened, and finalize lets a non-zero recorded status outrank a SIGTERM that arrived after it (probe (iii)-c: BEFORE 'scheduler termination ... failcount left at 0'; AFTER 'the loop had already exited rc=1 when the SIGTERM arrived -- counting the failure, not the signal', failcount 1). A recorded 143 past the runtime floor is deliberately NOT caught by that rule and stays a scheduler kill, so K1-K6 are unchanged. CLOSED (c): the loop writes $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed after every cycle whose five stages returned 0, the wrapper reads it at entry and in finalize, and a link that advanced it clears the failure run in both the scheduler-termination branch and the failure branch. KTG_MAX_FAILS=3 therefore means three failures with no completed cycle between them, which is what the header always claimed. Scenario O re-run with a cycle-recording loop gives 1,0,0,1,0,1 and does not trip; re-run with a loop that records nothing it still gives 1,1,1,2,2,3 and trips, as before. DOCUMENTED, not changed (d): KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, KTG_MAX_FAILS and KTG_MAX_CHAIN read the job environment and Slurm's default --export=ALL carries them down the whole chain; that is how an operator retunes a running chain without editing a file under a live job, so they stay knobs and the operating rule -- submit the first link from a clean shell -- is written next to them. KTG_RC_SIGTERM and KTG_RC_SCRATCH_STOP remain hard-coded. WHAT REMAINS OPEN, all reproduced in the same run: (r1) a loop status 143 arriving after KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it (probe (ii)-c) -- only Slurm job state can settle it, which is o25's; (r2) SCHED_TERM still outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that happens after the signal, so probe (i)-c is booked as a scheduler termination and the successor self-corrects in one extra link (probe Ic2 counts it 1/3 and cancels its own successor); (r3) a signal landing in the two statements between the loop's return and the LOOP_RC/LOOP_RC_SET assignments is still read as a walltime end -- the window is irreducible without a lock and the direction is the safe one; (r4) the consequence of (c): a link that completes at least one cycle and then fails never accumulates, so a crash loop that manages a full cycle per link is bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN=200 and not by the breaker (probe P5, count oscillating 2,2,2 over three links). | o34_loop_script_errexit_lost_under_bash_invocation | codes/loop/loop.sbatch:455 launches the loop as `bash "$LOOP_SH" ...`, and options on a shebang line are ignored when a script is run that way, so synchronous_loop_9x9.sh's `#!/bin/bash -eu` (:1) is inert under the wrapper: only `set -o pipefail` (:2) is in force at start, errexit is switched on for the first time at :232 (`set -e` after the first cycle's scratch-guard call) and nounset never. Reproduced by the validator (evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair2_harness.txt, Part 2 and the shebang probe in validation_repair2.md section 3): a stand-in loop with -eu only in its shebang kept running after its killed child and returned 0, and `printf '#!/bin/bash -eu\nfalse\necho reached' > p.sh; bash p.sh` prints 'reached' with errexit=off nounset=off, exit 0, while ./p.sh exits 1. Exposure: the archive-staging section :44-228 -- realpath/git rev-parse, mkdir, the cp of python/*.py, python/katago, python/muon, the katago binary, the two wrappers and the two configs into $DATED_ARCHIVE, git show/diff into version.txt, the .exported and .tmp sweeps and `cd "$DATED_ARCHIVE"` -- runs unguarded, so a failed copy or cd is followed by cycle 1 out of a wrong or incomplete archive instead of the exit 2 the header comment :11-12 ('-eu + pipefail are kept so any stage failure still stops the loop') and the o17 comment :157-159 ('under bash -eu the stock copy kills cycle 1') promise; every explicit `exit 2` check (:64, :72, :89, :145, :165) still works, and stage failures inside the while loop still stop the loop because :232 is reached before the first stage. Fix shape: `set -eu -o pipefail` at :2 of synchronous_loop_9x9.sh (upstream relies on the shebang because it executes the script directly), or exec the script directly from the wrapper; then remove the now-redundant `set -e` at :232 only if the `set +e` at :229 is kept for the guard call. Closes when `sed -n 2p codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh` shows both -e and -u, the KTG_STAGE_ONLY=1 dry run still exits 0, `bash codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh` with a deliberately unreadable $KTG_CODES/cfg/selfplay_9x9.cfg still exits 2 (explicit check) and with a failing `cp` in the staging section exits non-zero instead of starting a cycle, and the loop_resume section 2 check still exits 0. | discharged | yes | r_loop_resume_under_walltime_static | worker loop_resume_under_walltime | arxiv-1902.10565::loop_resume_under_walltime |
| o35_chain_state_files_unvalidated | The chain state files under $BASEDIR are consumed by arithmetic without a plain-decimal check. codes/loop/loop.sbatch:144 and :232 accept any .cycles_completed matching *[0-9]* and feed it to $(( cycles_now - CYCLES_AT_ENTRY )) at :233; codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh:310-311 does the same with $(( CYCLES_DONE + 1 )); loop.sbatch:139 reads .failcount with no check at all. Reproduced by the validator (evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair3_harness.txt S4, S5, S6, R7c): with .cycles_completed = 08 and .failcount = 2, a failing link prints 'loop.sbatch: line 233: 08: value too great for base', finalize() is abandoned at that line, .failcount stays 2, no .breaker_tripped is written and the queued successor is NOT cancelled -- the o26 class, a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN=200 because the count never advances; the loop script itself prints 'line 311: 08: value too great for base' and exits 1 after every completed cycle, leaving the file at 08. With .failcount = abc the wrapper prints 'line 311: abc: unbound variable' inside finalize() and exits without writing the count, successor queued. Values abc, '', -1, 1e3, 0x10 read as 0 as designed; 007 reads as octal 7; an integer past 2^63 wraps silently. Only the loop writes .cycles_completed and only finalize() writes .failcount, neither with a leading zero, so the exposure needs a hand-edited or foreign-written file. Fix shape: read the counters through 10#, e.g. $(( 10#$cycles_now - 10#$CYCLES_AT_ENTRY )) and $(( 10#$CYCLES_DONE + 1 )), or strip leading zeros in the case guard; validate .failcount at :139 with the same case pattern and reset it to 0 with a logged line when it is not a plain decimal. Closes by a re-run of S4 (all seeds), S5 and S6 in which finalize() writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the successor for every seed, and the loop records the next cycle for 08. | open | no | — | worker loop_resume_under_walltime | arxiv-1902.10565::loop_resume_under_walltime; arxiv-1902.10565::loop_failure_circuit_breaker |
